rationale: A wins because it gives the founder four usable beat shapes without forcing the facts to do circus tricks. "What 6,000 Consumer Brands Buying Grocery Ads Reveals About Where CPG Money Is Moving" has a real buyer-protagonist lens; B's "The carts that skip checkout could be feeding the ad engine that just crossed $1 billion" is interesting, but it is still an inference wearing a headline. B even admits "nothing in the facts confirms smart-cart data feeds ad targeting," which is honest, but not pitch-ready.
gaps_in_A: "The $1B threshold is a widely recognized milestone in the retail media category" imports outside context the update did not supply. It may be true, but this judge only gets the supplied facts.
"as digital attribution has gotten harder" is a real-world trend claim, not a fact in the update. Useful if sourced, sloppy if left as decoration.
The retail-media angle and the CPG-spend angle both ride "$1B" plus "6,000 consumer brands." They are distinct enough, but only if the proof separates category ranking from buyer behavior.
"delivery growth stalls to single digits" sharpens "slowed to single digits" into a more dramatic verb. Get the actual percentage before building the contrarian story on that word.
gaps_in_B: "delivery growth is stalling" overstates the supplied fact. Single-digit growth can be ugly or merely mature; without the exact number, "stalling" is playing dress-up.
"More grocery chains are letting Instacart's smart carts run their checkout line" overclaims what the facts say. The carts skip the checkout line; they do not necessarily run the checkout operation.
"taking over a function — checkout — that used to be entirely in-house" drags in staffing and operating-model implications the update does not prove.

"More grocery chains are letting Instacart's smart carts run their checkout line" and "Instacart's smart-cart rollout turns it into checkout infrastructure for grocery chains" are too close. Collapse them or make one about retailer operations and the other about Instacart's revenue model with real commercial proof.
